en: Udāna 8.10 Dutiyadabbasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!”
“Venerable Sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“Bhikkhus, Dabba Mallaputta, having ascended into the air and into the sky, sat cross-legged in the firmament.”
Having sat down, he entered the fire-element, and having emerged from it, when his body had attained final Nirvana,
as it was burning and being consumed, neither ash nor soot could be discerned. Just as, for example, when ghee or oil is burning and being consumed, neither ash nor soot can be discerned.
"In the very same way, monks, when Dabba Mallaputta had risen into the air,
sat cross-legged in the sky, entered the fire-element, emerged from it, and attained final Nibbāna,
as his body was burning and being consumed, neither ash nor soot could be found."
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
"Just like a blazing fire struck by an iron bar..."
Just as the destination of one who has gradually attained peace is not known,
so it is with those who are rightly liberated.
There is no way to describe the attainment of those who have crossed over the flood of the bonds of sensual desire and reached unshakable happiness.
The tenth.
The eighth chapter, the Pāṭaligāmiya-vagga.
Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
Four [offerings] leading to Nibbāna were spoken for Cunda at Pāṭaligāma;
two paths were spoken for Visākhā.
"Together with Dabba, they are ten.
This is the summary verse for the sections in the *Udāna*.
This first section is "The Supreme Awakening."
This second is the Mucalinda Chapter;
the third is the excellent Nandaka Chapter,
and the fourth is the excellent Meghiya Chapter.
Here, Soṇa is the foremost in the fifth chapter;
the one born blind is the foremost in the sixth chapter;
and Cūḷa is the foremost in the seventh chapter.
The eighth chapter on Pāṭaligāma.
This well-arranged group of eight contains no fewer than eighty excellent suttas.
This has been shown by the Stainless One who possesses vision;
indeed, they have called this "an Utterance" (udāna).
The Udāna-pāḷi is finished.
